decisions.rationale: Valid: nothing in the module records where the required 30 lab minutes run on Standard, and the intake's Lab plan (authoring/evidence/spring-boot/intake.md) still describes spring-boot-basics as having no lab and S9/S12 as the only required Standard labs. The frozen calendar (curriculum/snapshot/pep-calendar.json dayTypes.Concept) gives every Concept day a 40-minute 'Faded, then fresh problem' block whose evolvFormat is coding lab, the same block html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async uses for its required Concept-day lab. Day fit at S2, checked against the topic.json budgets: the pages total 58 (15+13+15+15). No S2 topic has a video-artifact.md, so the pages may use the Short video block, as the collections-streams intake does. They fill Reading 15 + Short video 8 + Worked example 12 + Short exercises 20 = 55 and 3 minutes of the 40-minute block. The remaining 37 hold the up-to-15-minute practice mastery check and the 22 task minutes. Warm-up 8, Mini-quiz 7 and Reflection 10 are unchanged, so the day totals 120 with zero slack. No existing record places the S2 mastery check; this note sets it inside the same block, matching its instructions ('before the module coding lab'). As in the html-css-js precedent, the 8-minute one-time online setup is done before the block. Fix, in scope: add this sentence verbatim to sourceCoverageNotes in authoring/catalog/spring-boot/spring-boot-basics/module.json, directly after the existing module-coding-lab note: "Standard placement: the required module coding lab runs on S2 in the frozen Concept-day 40-minute 'Faded, then fresh problem' coding-lab block (curriculum/snapshot/pep-calendar.json dayTypes.Concept), after the four S2 pages and the practice mastery check. Authoring estimate, not piloted, with no slack: no S2 topic links a video, so the four pages (58 minutes) fill Reading, Short video, Worked example and Short exercises (55) and 3 minutes of that block, the check takes up to 15 and the lab's 22 task minutes fill the remaining 22, so S2 stays at 120 minutes; the one-time online setup (mvn -q dependency:go-offline, about 8 minutes) is done before the block, as in html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async. The lab sits outside the calendar's lab overlay, because S2 is a Concept day with requiredLab false, but inside a Concept-day block whose calendar format is coding lab. This supersedes the intake's no-lab statement for spring-boot-basics (authoring/evidence/spring-boot/intake.md, section Lab plan), which is left for a course-level follow-up branch." The intake text is course-level evidence that this module branch may not edit. The operator reports the stale intake Lab plan sentences to the supervisor as a course-level follow-up and does not edit them here.

Valid: README.md (sha256 8797a1c7...) does not tell learners that the lab is required on Standard and not required on Fast, and it gives no day, block or time. The sibling required labs and the html-css-js precedent all state this. The fix is a Goal sentence in README.md. The published learner repository JesterCharles/pep-standard-spring-boot-spring-boot-basics-lab mirrors that README byte for byte, so editing it on this branch would make the published repo drift from source, and changing the learner repo is outside this branch's authority. The catalog sentence from spring-basics-req-edu-001 records the status and placement for authors only; learners never see it. Decision needed from the supervisor (firstmate/captain): either authorize a README Goal sentence plus a matching sync PR to the published learner repo, for example 'Standard track, S2 (a Concept day), in its 40-minute Faded, then fresh coding-practice block; required on Standard, about 22 minutes, with the one-time setup done before the block; Fast Track skips this lab.' (that edit re-stales lab-run.json and the critic bindings, so bundle it with the README fix for spring-basics-req-sme-001), or accept that the README stays silent and the platform shows the track requirement.

Valid, confirmed against the README and pages (the path-query page teaches a required query parameter and asks for the 400 when it is missing; the response-codes page's editor activity checks a noContent DELETE): Task 4 binds only an optional query parameter (required = false), and no task binds a required one. Task 1 replaces one manual new in the controller with constructor injection of a configured catalog bean; the lab has no service or repository layer to wire. The core skills are practiced, so this is recorded as partial coverage. The lab is not grown, which keeps the 22-minute task budget and avoids lab byte changes that would reopen the solved run, critic bindings and the mirrored learner repo. The gaps are covered elsewhere: path-query-and-body-parameters#o2 (missing required query parameter) is in the mastery-check blueprint objectives and on the page, and porting-and-configuration/coding-lab claims constructor-injection-across-layers#o1 on S3-S4. The same sentence also adds the catalog note that the open recheck item spring-practice-edu-008 asks for; that finding's earlier accept in module-practice-reconciliation.json stands. Fix, in scope: add this sentence verbatim to sourceCoverageNotes in authoring/catalog/spring-boot/spring-boot-basics/module.json, after the placement sentence from spring-basics-req-edu-001: "Partial objective coverage in the module coding lab (recorded, no lab change): for path-query-and-body-parameters#o1 it binds a path variable, an optional query parameter and a JSON body but no required query parameter, which the page and the practice mastery check (path-query-and-body-parameters#o2) cover; for dependency-injection-replacing-manual-wiring#o1 it replaces one manual new in the controller with constructor injection of a configured bean, and wiring across controller, service and repository layers is taught by constructor-injection-across-layers and applied in the porting-and-configuration module lab on S3-S4; for response-codes-with-responseentity#o1 it practices 200, 201 with Location and 404 but not 204, which the page's editor activity (a DELETE handler returning noContent), the mastery-check feedback and the graded course final cover."

Valid, and confirmed empirically. On 2026-11-19 the solved-run operator worked in private staging with an empty local repository and ran only the documented setup (mvn -q dependency:go-offline). The documented spot check mvn -q -o spring-boot:run then exited 1 with "No plugin found for prefix 'spring-boot'". This matches the critic's static reading: starter/pom.xml lists only maven-surefire-plugin under build/plugins and does not declare spring-boot-maven-plugin, the parent declares spring-boot-maven-plugin only in pluginManagement, and go-offline resolves only build plugins. README line 88, expected/test-summary.txt line 12 and the Offline note, which says only setup uses the network, are therefore wrong for a clean learner machine. The required test command mvn -q -o test is unaffected: the starter fails the 5 declared tests and the private solved overlay passes 5/5 silently. Every fix changes bytes mirrored to the published learner repo: (a) add spring-boot-maven-plugin, with its version inherited from the parent, to the existing build/plugins in starter/pom.xml, or (b) drop -o from the spot check in README.md and expected/test-summary.txt and say that the first run downloads the plugin. Either one is outside this branch's authority. The critic reports that none of the seven Spring lab poms declares the plugin, so the choice is also course-wide. Decision needed from the supervisor (firstmate/captain): choose (a) or (b) for this lab and the other Spring labs, and authorize the source edit plus a sync PR to JesterCharles/pep-standard-spring-boot-spring-boot-basics-lab, followed by a fresh solved run, a spot check on an empty local repository and a critic rebind. Reconciler's recommendation is (a): it keeps the lab-contract promise that everything after setup runs offline, and the Offline note stays true without new wording. Medium severity, so this escalation does not block the required-lab change; the required test path is proven.

Valid: a local Surefire 3.x plain-text report (outside this repo, checked 2026-11-19) begins with a dashed separator, a 'Test set: <class>' line and a second separator. The 'Tests run: N, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0' line comes fourth, followed by ', Time elapsed: <n> s -- in <class>'. So 'begins:' in expected/test-summary.txt line 9 is literally inaccurate. Low impact, because the pass signal the README teaches is silence plus exit status 0. The fix is a wording change in expected/, which the published learner repo mirrors byte for byte, so it is outside this branch's authority. Decision needed from the supervisor (firstmate/captain): authorize changing 'begins:' to 'contains the line:' (with the time-elapsed suffix noted), batched with the README or pom fix for spring-basics-req-sme-001 and the matching learner-repo sync PR, or accept the wording as is.
